. what if the drive itself , the physical drive , goes toast ? you 're stuck unless you pay money . thus the value of having external media for restoration if and when that were to happen . the ssd bar in the air is replaceable , and there are already options from owc for those users . but it 's useless unless you pay 30 to download lion and burn it write it yourself or pay apple 70 for a usb stick with lion on it . to me both are unacceptable alternatives for something that should be in the box of every computer . mac_os x 10 . 7 , code name lion i want to interject here and state for the record that the majority of what bothers me with this purchase really has more to do with lion , the newest operating system from the apple , rather than the air hardware itself . based on my experience , the lion os is a step in the wrong direction . apple is attempting to blend what we know of mac_os with what certain users know of ios , and the output is a very clunky experience at times . they introduced plenty of new features , and changed some tried and true features at the same time . it 's clear they are attempting to create a single os for both tablets and the desktop os , but it 's just ... wrong . apple introduced a new feature , mission_control , which is designed to act as the evolution of expos and spaces . the problem is that mission_control is finicky . it wants each app to be run in full screen to be able to separate them correctly within a single desktop . however ... running apps full screen is a bit of a pain because it disables the dock . thus if you 're running firefox , let 's say , in full screen you ca n't then see the unread count on mail in the dock . this basically forces you to run a desktop that is just a desktop and then run other apps in their own desktop space . if you do n't run apps in full screen , mission_control then just " paper stacks " them in a very unorganized fashion within the same desktop . if an app is minimized into the dock , it does not show in mission_control . this seems bass ackwards ... if it is minimized into the dock it should be one of the icons on top in mission_control automatically . the only way to force this is to manually create the desktop and assign the app to it , or full screen the app and then switch out of it . i know that 's hard to understand , but the bottom line is that the approach is n't very well implemented . apple has introduced another feature , launchpad , which is essentially an ipad view of all of the local applications . it supports the grouping concept also found on ios . anyone who owns an ipod touch or an ipad iphone will instantly recognize this . the idea is obvious the concept of it just does not work on a full computer . it translates on a simple touch_interface , but not a computer where you 're not really touching . it should be obvious that the intent is to have one operating system for both desktops and tablets in an attempt to extend ios beyond its limitations and dumb down the desktop experience . i get it . but beyond the obvious issues , there are more functional problems . launchpad shows queued up downloads or updates to existing apps rather than the app itself . so for example , i saw there was an upgrade for iphoto and started it from the app_store when i was on the plane . but when i saw it was over 600mb i stopped it . problem is that made iphoto unavailable from launchpad because it changed to a download prompt instead of the app . it 's not a deal_breaker , as one could go to the applications folder by exiting launchpad or not using it , but it 's something to note ... apple 's got some work to do . " natural scrolling " is a joke . it turns over 20 years of computing on its head and not in a good way . i turned that stuff off the moment i saw it . for those that do n't know what this is , apple has set the default scroll behavior to where the window will scroll in the same direction as where you scroll your fingers mouse . so for example , right now if you scroll a window down , the the page will go up so you read down the page . that 's logical . in the default scroll of lion , if you do the same downward scroll , the page will move down . so if you want to read towards the bottom like normal people , you would scroll up , because you 're " pulling the page up " in order to read downwards . if it sounds confusing , it is . i disabled this immediately . those who are on the fence about this , think of this way . if i asked you to get to the bottom of the stairs , what direction are you moving ? down . down bottom . that 's logical , right ? so when looking at a piece of paper , if i wanted to go to the bottom of the page , i am reading down the page . the analogy i stated before of " move the paper up to read downwards " works if my hands are directly on the paper . but when i am not touching the paper , my eyes go down the paper itself , say if laying on table , goes up . that 's why computer based scrolling has worked for over two decades . it 's designed to work for your eyes , not for your hands . " natural scrolling " makes perfect sense on an ipad , because you 're " touching the paper " directly , thus you would move the paper so that you can get to the next parts of what you 're reading . i did n't find it to translate well on a disconnected input medium like the trackpad at all . your mileage may vary , but in my opinion it 's more clunky than it 's worth , and i would rather it had been disabled by default , with options for users who want to try that input type that are converts from the ipad . lion wants to remember open_tabs by default in safari . so let 's say you have 3 tabs_open and you shut the browser down because you 're finished . in my mind if i close all three tabs it 's because i 'm done using them and the next time i open the browser i expect a clean slate otherwise i would just use bookmarks . in lion , by default , when you open the browser multiple_times , it will reopen whatever tabs you had open the last time you ran it . even reset safari does not stop this behavior . you have to disable it in system preferences if you do n't want it . lion has taken a questionable direction with regards to design strategy . it feels very much like apple 's strategy was to create an os that could be used on both a computer and a tablet , and i 'd be shocked if we did n't see a lion version of the ipad down the road . the problem is a lot of the features just do n't translate well to a computer environment at all , yet would feel right at home on a tablet . things like rotating and the new mail interface . i know some people have reported things as bugs with lion ... i do n't think they are . i think a lot of what we are experiencing are intentional changes ... and anyone who thinks it 's a bug , is really feeling the negative impacts of the changes . call a spade a spade . in summary ... do i recommend it ? that 's a big yes . the 2011 air is a solid machine that imo is hindered somewhat by a questionable os design . the hardware is spot on and what the air really should have been in the 2010 revision . the backlight keyboard adds significant value to the air , and the 2011 just feels right . the base 13 " is a great value and well worth the money you spend on it . it 's not going to replace a pro for many reasons . but it 's strong enough to be someone 's primary if they really want it to be . the review may sound like it 's lower than a_4 , but the more critical negatives are with lion , not with the air itself . the air itself is rock solid . it 's a strong value and well worth the dollars you spend on it . the higher_end 13 " is pushing it in terms of true value , as is the low_end 11 " , but the high end 11 " and the base 13 " both are the best values in the apple lineup right now . the 13 " pro has a stronger processor but not by much , and you must add a ssd to make it slightly superior to the base air . that 's the way it should have been from the get go . value , people . value .

improvements and the performance gain is much less dramatic ( the main exception being the much faster ssd ) . if you 're trying to decide between an air and a 13 " macbook_pro the air is way thinner_and_lighter than the pro , so it 's much nicer to travel with . the air 's display has higher_resolution than the pro 's . the air 's ssd blows away the pro 's sluggish 5400 rpm hard_drive . between applications by using cmd tab but it does not automatically bring up the other application , it just changes the active application in menu_bar ( if the application was minimized ) . i never understood the reasoning behind this , why would i just want to see the menu_bar of the other application , i cannot imagine doing anything just with a menu_bar . after some search on the internet i found the work around to do this in os x . the answer is to press cmd tab followed by the option key ( just before releasing the cmd key ) to switch between the applications perfectly . you can also scroll your four fingers on the track pad to bring up all the applications and then highlight the application you want to choose to change the active application window . it is simply irritating to switch between keyboard and the track pad when you are typing some document or email . you can also use one of the function key buttons instead of using the four fingers but at the end of the day windows 7 does a great_job here . please do note that you can only switch directly between applications but not directly to the active window of an application when you used cmd tab , for example you cannot switch directly to a second excel workbook , you have to bring up the application first and only then switch to the second workbook . i am aware that there is software available ( namely witch for 14 ) to do this but i already paid for the machine and why should i go through all this trouble and change the system registry entries to simply switch between applications . update we can also use spaces and assign some shortcuts to spaces ( like option arrow ) to make the switch between applications easier but you need to assign a different space to every application and this could be tedious after some time . also the animations could make you dizzy after a while . switching within an application to switch between the various windows of the same application , the answer is to everything from casual_web_browsing to video_editing . speed and performance advantage macbook airapart from the hard_drives and port configurations , the technology inside the machines is virtually identical in both the newly refreshed macbook air and macbook pro . both pros and airs come with either i5 or i7 intel " ivy bridge " processors , intel_hd_graphics_4000 , usb 3 . 0 , and lightning fast thunderbolt ports . while the macbook air models are at a disadvantage to the macbook_pro models in terms of cpu clock speeds , any performance disadvantage from the processor_speed is more than made up for by the lightning fast performance of the air 's ssd hard_drive , which apple markets as " flash " storage . in everyday_tasks from gaming to web_browsing to watching flash movies and editing video , the macbook air is faster significantly_faster in virtually every task . the air boots up in less than 12 seconds while the pro takes upwards of one minute . screen advantage macbook aironce you get used to the super_high_resolution 1440 x 900 led display on the macbook air , the 1280 x 800 back lit led display on the macbook pro looks downright grainy and primitive . simply put , the resolution would matter , the graphics look grainy and pixelated , which just is n't acceptable for a pro level laptop in 2012 . upgradability advantage macbook proone major difference that 's important to consider between the air and the pro is that the pro is more flexible and adaptable in terms of upgradability . with only a screw_driver and about 10 minutes of your time , you can add more memory to the pro , replace the hard_drive , and even add a second hard_drive in place of the optical_disc drive . the air , on the other hand , is stuck in the configuration you purchase it in except that you can opt to replace the ssd " flash " hard_drive with a higher_capacity drive . however , both the air and pro have usb 3.0 ( which is five times faster than usb 2.0 and you want to add your own ssd to this laptop or increase the amount of ram . any hardware modification to this laptop will void it 's warranty . if you go to the lenovo forums and to this page t5 ideapad y u v and z series new u400 general td p 580903there is a thread on hardware modding this laptop and on page 2 , there is a link to a lenovo website with videos on how to take this laptop apart . note that taking this laptop apart is very difficult and much harder than it seems in the video . note the hard_drive bay in the lenovo u400 can not fit a traditional ssd and can only fit hdd . this is because a usb port intrudes upon the space for the hard_drive and the traditional hard_drive has a small space above the sata and power connectors where there is n't anything to obstruct the ssd unfortunately has a lip . in order to fit a ssd you pretty much only have three choices 1 . disassemble your ssd and tape it into to laptop . 2 . disassemble your ssd and cut off a corner of it 's case with a power_tool . 3 . purchase a msata_ssd and install that alongside your hdd . i went with option 2 4 . purchase a height 7mm_ssd ex . samsung 830 ( will still need to tape ssd ) . doing a clean_install of windows_7 did not work for me installing drivers became a nightmare . recovery_disk can be used unfortunately your laptop does n't come with one . upgrading ramyou only have easy_access to one of two memory slots . the second slot requires some serious hardware disassembly included the removal of the entire motherboard . luckily , the 2gb_memory chip is on the side that is easy to access . however , having two separate memory chips from different companies on the same system may cause instability and occasional crashes . which happened when i upgraded the stock 2gb samsung to a 4gb corsair . i would suggest purchasing a single 4gb samsung stick of the same model as the one in the computer . it 'll make your life easier . how to take apart the laptop watch the lenovo support videos . 1 . take off two rubber feet the ones in the back next to the monitor hinge . i used a flat head screwdriver with its head covered with a microfiber cloth ( to prevent scratches ) to pry the feet off . 2 . unscrew two screws under the rubber feet . 3 . pull the bottom cover towards the back of the laptop ( back where the monitor hinge is ) . you only need to pull it about 2mm . gently lift the back of the bottom plate while pulling towards you . the back should pop out of the clips with some patience . be careful not bend the part of the back of the bottom cover that bends up along side the monitor hinge . after releasing the back and side clips . while pulling the cover to slide it off , also lift the front of the back cover gently . this part is the most difficult and i enlisted the help of a friend . i had my friend gently tap the front of the bottom cover with a hammer on top of the back of a screw_driver that was covered with some gauze pads .. while he was tapping , i gently pulled the front of the bottom cover away from the laptop . 4 . once the cover is removed the rest is self explanatory . 5 . putting the cover back on . put the cover back on with the front first . the rest of the clips should click into place as you push down . afterwards , slide the bottom cover towards the front of the laptop . while pulling , screw the two screws back in . this part was easy and i was able to do it without enlisting help . if you have trouble lining up the two screw holes you may have bent the back of the bottom cover , you will have to bend them back into place with your hands or pry them back into place with a flat head screw_driver . random stuff it took me about 4 hours to finish my hardware modifications the first time . i also made alot of mistakes and ended up with a few chips . my second and third time opening up the computer took me about 10 minutes each . attempting to get the computer to work and install all the when one contacts the better business to complain about a company , nobody thinks the complaint is inappropriate , even though the company presumably makes many products or provides various services , and one is complaining about only one product or service ( presumably ) . the issue in the complaint is the company itself , not the specific product or service . so , here i tell you about a related laptop from lenovo and the type of experience i had . in fact , i am now catching lenovo in mid deceive the customer cycle , as the g570 is the " new model " of the g560 series 067999u laptop , which already has some devastating reviews which you might well miss if you turn here first . in brief , one of the tricks that lenovo pulls is to put out a computer that will not last even 2 years , then retire the product before the majority of negative_reviews pour in . so , it 's always a new day for lenovo , a company that eludes the consequences of its business " model . " i have a lenovo ideapad y550p . it started falling apart in its first year , when the front of the dvd cd tray came off . i had such trouble getting through to " support " that i gave up . after all , the problem was more cosmetic than anything , and i did n't use the dvd cd tray much . but just a few weeks back ( after about 1.5 years of use ) , the battery developed a bizarre problem and would not charge . no , this is n't the usual battery wear out which occurs gradually . in addition , it seems that the usb ports are also failing . now , i am pretty good with computers . the way i keep them up , they typically last so long that i just toss them . it 's not that hard control power surges run software that corrects hardware and software problems early on and so on . i have never had a machine go bad on me before two years , except once , when it was bad out of the box . but my problem with the " ideapad " line is apparently common enough . if you have a problem , you will have a fairly poor chance of finally getting anyone in lenovo " support . " when the 1 year period is over , you will be told that lenovo has no record of your purchase , and , after a long series of holds on the phone , you will be directed to the retailer ( in my case , newegg ) who sold you the machine ( ? ! ? ) . i managed to get newegg to initiate a case with lenovo , but lenovo then proceeded to ignore newegg . i have had good computers and bad ones . i have dealt with good support staff and lousy staff . but i have never dealt with such a sleazy manufacturer . i will not recommend another company , but i will urge you to avoid buying lenovo before , like me , you become an another unhappy customer . ( update 1 24 2012 ) i see from the comments that while some people totally understand the reasoning behind my review ( thanks ! ) , a couple complain that i did not review the precise model of lenovo for sale here , " just " the company . of course , my point was lenovo has a " business_model " evidently based on producing poor machines , and that it protects itself from the consequences by manipulating the typical customer review system , withdrawing machines before the negative_reviews get too numerous , only to replace these withdrawn machines with new poor ones , thus continuing the cycle , always one step ahead of honest assessment . in a nutshell , my point was that this bad tree will not produce good fruit , except by some fluke . those who want to endorse this business_model are free to squander their money . by the way , that one commentator has this exact machine and is happy with it now does not mean that he will be happy with it in the near future . i , too , was happy with my lenovo in the beginning .

another thing which i did to reclaim an additional 10 gb of useful space was to eliminate the recovery_partition , and then expand the main partition to fill up that empty space . that is easily done in the disk_management utility . type diskmgmt . msc into the run box on the start_menu , or winlogo r , right click on the recovery_partition and select delete . then right click on the main partition and select expand , and just use the default entries if you want to maximally utilize the hard_drive 's space , and click ok and you 'll see the " unallocated " partition disappear . now , of course , you will not be able to recover your computer to factory settings if you have done this , but , if you do a backup of the factory configuration as delivered , say with the acronis boot you will not have to go back and start over unless you really want to , which might be the case , if you just want a fresh installation , so be sure to make that initial backup , if you plan to reconnect the cd_rom drive , as it will revert to the ssd boot_drive at the top of the list . it only takes a few seconds to do that no big_deal . to conserve battery power , i recommend that you turn you see what i mean . zenbook does have much faster data transfer through its usb 3 port . it is easily multiple_times faster than macbook air 's usb 2 . but unless you routinely transfer very large_files , i 'm not sure if this is so important . also , macbook air has a thunderbolt port which i 've not tested in comparison with the zenbook . zenbook also uses a much faster ssd ( nearly twice as fast as that of the macbook air ) , but for some reason , i did not notice a very big difference in actual_performance . again , it 's probably because both are already superfast for daily tasks . gamers may tell a different story , but why do you buy an ultracompact laptop like these if you are a gamer ? ( 2 ) design and build_quality both computers are extremely well designed and well built . to me , the zenbook is almost a bit too pretty ( a bit too showy and trendy to my taste ) . this is usually a problem i have with mac products , but now , you 've got a windows product that beats that . i wish they would make a zenbook in all black , and with a more plain business looking ( but keep the feel of the high quality and compactness ) . had lenovo made a similar machine maintaining the basic black square edged thinkpad style with the same compactness and thermal performance ( see below ) , i would nearly certainly buy the thinkpad instead . but there 's nothing even in the radar screen on the thinkpad side , so i caved in . ( 4 ) two second instant_resume if you have got used to waiting for your windows to boot up , you 'd be pleasantly shocked by how zenbook manages to always wake up in 2 seconds , unless you 've done a cold shutdown . instant_resume was a famous feature of macbook air , but now zenbook completely matches ( perhaps even surpasses ) macbook air on that . asus designed a super hybrid engine which enables the zenbook to have a true 2 seocnd resume in the entire two weeks standby time . asus claims it is better than macbook air because macbook air 's instant_resume works only for a day of standby time , and after that would take 6 seconds to resume . i did not test that . but if you use your laptop on a daily basis , both these machines have reliable instant_resume , and you will appreciate this feature in your daily use . instant_resume is not just a cool feature . it is very practical and has a huge impact on user_experience . for example , without such instant_resume ability , a laptop would have to have a minimum of eight hours_of_battery_life to reliably last through a whole day without causing headaches . with instant_resume , a 5 hour_battery_life will last a whole day for most people in most situations . you usually do n't use the computer constantly every minute , and the reliable instant_resume of these computers makes a seamless whole day long user_experience with a single charge of a five hour_battery . for example , while i 'm traveling , i can set this laptop to go to sleep after every 5 min . of inactivity without feeling distracted . only a laptop that has instant_resume can work this way , or it will drive you crazy . in this situation , " instant " is the key word , and even a 5 second resume may feel bad by interrupting your natural workflow and you will most likely end up setting an auto sleep longer than a minimum of 30 min . instant_resume is therefore a crucial factor in the matter of intelligent power_management . ok i am not going to repeat all the positive comments but rather would like to post a solution which i came across . ok so some people commented about losing or dropping wireless connections . well it started to happen to me to . now i am it security professional and at first i was checking patches etc . then i read a genius comment which is so simple and works . so here is the solution . do the following ( windows_7 ) 1 ) go to control panal2 ) choose network and sharing3 ) on the left_hand side choose " change adapter settings " 4 ) right click the wireless_network connection and choose properties ( it is the last option ) 5 ) choose the top option " client for microsoft networks " 6 ) choose configure on top7 ) go to the power_management tab8 ) de select " allow the computer to turn off the device to save power " save and close . i did some additional analysis of this issue there is one additional step you need to do . 9 ) go to control_panel and power options10 ) the default is balanced choose change plan settings11 ) on the bottom choose change advanced plan settings12 ) scroll to wireless adapter settings and click the plus sign to the left of it to expand the options . 13 ) now click the second plus sign power_saver mode14 ) click on the the battery option and a selection box will open_set both battery and plugged in to maximum performance . save and close all . this should solve the issue once and for all . what was happening the power_saver option was shutting down the wireless adapter to save power thus the unreliable connections . if the connection is not constant it was shutting it down . the setting is effected by these two places . problem_solved ) happy computing

first of all , this is a very good computer , but not without a few tweaks . that 's why i only gave it 4 stars . secondly , anybody who thinks this computer is slow due to hardware does n't know what they 're talking about . this computer comes with a 1.0 to 1.3 ghz_dual_core processor , 3gb ddr3 ram ( some of which is used for graphics ) and a very nice gpu ( graphics_processing_unit . ) it 's more than equipped to handle a modern operating system . the problem with it is the operating system that is installed by default windows_7_home_premium 64 bit . this computer is on the low_end system specs for win7 64 bit and will not run it very well . why ? because win7 64 bit is beast of an os . on paper , it requires a 1.0 ghz_processor , 2gb_ram and a decent gpu . in reality , it requires about twice the processing_power and ram because it not only runs 64 bit software but it also runs an emulator that allows you to run 32 bit software . so , in reality , it 's working 1.5 to 2 times as hard . the people who built this computer know this , yet they still put 64 bit windows on it . but , this is a common_problem , all of the pc manufacturers are doing it for the low_end systems because they 'll technically run win7 64 bit . on top of the heavy os , asus has also included all of those " helpful " little utilities that run in the background . all those do is slow down the computer even further . the power4gear utility , for example , is totally useless unless you want to save battery power at the expense of performance . all it does is slow down your fans so that the battery wo n't run down as quickly , so the computer runs hotter and compensates by slowing down . it 's useless , it should be removed . by removing it , you 're no longer limiting the fan speeds . now , there are basically two options that will speed up this system . option 1 is a hardware upgrade . you can put a faster_processor and more ram in the computer . however , this presents two problems . first , you 'll void your warranty doing so . second , the radeon hd 6290 gpu is designed to work specifically with the c 60 processor and uses the processor to improve its performance . if you replace the processor , you 'll be hurting the hd 6290 . besides , if you 're going to put money into this thing right off the bat , you might as well have just paid more for a higher_end computer . option 2 is what i did and it wo n't void your warranty you can simply replace windows_7_home_premium 64 bit with something else . personally , i chose windows_7_home_premium 32 bit because 32 bit win7 will run on about half the system resources of 64 bit and because i have the windows_7_home_premium retail release for my desktop and it has both dvds . first , i created my factory default dvds ( it took 4 dvds ) and then i went to asus 's website and got the 32 bit drivers . then i popped in my win7 32 bit dvd and reinstalled it . i used the oem product_key from the bottom of the laptop ( because i use the other license on my desktop ) and it accepted it . it mulled over it for a while , but it worked_great . now i 'm running_windows 7 32 bit on this laptop and it 's running a lot better . there are less pauses before it performs a task and it performs tasks more quickly . this is the os that asus should have put on here , but they did n't . i also installed lubuntu ( linux ) 12 . 04 32 bit as a 2nd os and set up a dual_boot . since lubuntu is very lightweight , it runs very smoothly on this laptop . so , all in all , this is a very good laptop . the hardware is very good , i love the radeon hd 6290 graphics . it 's good for videos and i 've even gotten a few games to run on it . most of them are older_games , but i have gotten star trek online running on the laptop on low graphics_settings and that game is only 2 years old . so , anything is possible once you tweak this laptop a bit .

about me network security analyst , hobbyist photographer , casual_gamer . overview1 . summary2 . design3 . performance4 . limits5 . expresscache explanation1 . summarythis is the section if you just want to hear the answer to your question should i buy it . i would say yes . at a 700 this laptop is quite a gem . you are getting macbook air type performance for nearly 500 less . the only argument against buying this is if you need a larger screen than 14 " or you need an extreme battery endurance laptop ( the series 5 gets 5 realistic hours ) 2 . designthe laptop is sleek and attractive . it has a nice gunmetal finish and smooth , round corners . the heat vent is located on the back of the laptop to keep your table ( or legs ) cool . the design is simple and classy . the screen is matte , which displays better in sunlight but loses the " wow " factor of seeing your reflection in a glossy_screen . a backlit_keyboard would have been a nice touch . 3 . performancethe laptop packs a low_voltage , core_i5 dual_core_processor , 4gb_ddr3 ram , a 500 gb 5400rpm_hard_drive and a 16gb solid_state_drive . windows_7 is snappy and responsive . after using the laptop for three days for everything from diablo_3 to photoshop , the laptop can reliably get 5 hours battery_life under web_browsing , youtube videos and word_processing . i was able to manage 100 16mp photos in photoshop for a little over 4 hours . i upgraded the ram to 8gb by adding a 4gb_ddr3 module . be sure to cut the power to the laptop via the " emergency hole " before you add the module . i recommend purchasing low_voltage ram to offset the additional energy the occupied slot will use . i also used the free space on the ssd ( which is equal to 14 minus your gigs_of_ram ) to install diablo_3 . this can be done by going into disk_management , deleting the unallocated space on " disk 1 " , then creating a 'new simple volume' with the free space . another recommended upgrade is the harddrive . swapping in a 7200rpm energy saving drive will increase battery_life as well as response time . if you want to ugrade to a full ssd even better , but that is a bit too much . 4 . limitsthis is not a laptop for gamers with lack of a discrete video_card or a processor geared toward gaming , you will have to put up with medium_settings . the system maxes out at 8gb which means the most you can do is add 4gb to the only bay . the laptop 's casing can also dent easily if you 're not careful , so this is not for a rugged user looking for a computer they can throw in their bag . lack of a backlit_keyboard may also deter people who bring their laptops to bed . for everyone else though , this laptop is excellent . unlike other ultrabooks , this has real storage_space of over 400gb , while still having ssd performance for up to 10gb of your favorite games and applications . 5 . explanation of expresscachei see a lot of reviews bashing expresscache out of ignorance , and i feel the need to explain it 's purpose here . first of all , one of the requirements for the official " ultrabook " label by intel is a small solid_state_drive for a hibernation partition . the idea is if you can reduce the time it takes to go in and out of hibernate , users will be more inclined to use it instead of sleep mode ( which drains battery_life while hibernate does not ) . this requires the ssd capacity to be equal to or greater than the system 's max amount of ram . with this notebook that leaves you at least 6gb on the ssd , if you have maxed the laptop at 8gb_ram . to make this space accessible for your storage ( there is no harm in doing it ) just follow my instructions provided above in performance .

when i got this xps_15z , was to remove the windows disk that came in it ( without ever turning it on ) and install a 120gb , high speed , low_power , ssd for my linux installation . this was not a simple task , since this laptop is so small and thin , doing something as simple as swapping the hard_disk , or replacing the battery , requires a somewhat complicated disassembly . fortunately , i found a guide on youtube that pointed out all the pitfalls as you 're going in . on the " small and thin " note ... it 's really quite cool . thin , light weight , covered with an aluminum titanium_alloy that looks nice but might scratch , and still large enough to hold a 15 " full 1920x1080 native glass led screen . i like the look and feel of the back lit keypad , but i 'm not crazy about the glide pad , but that 's ok , since i use a bluetooth mouse most of the time anyway . i 've seen many people knocking it because they say it looks like a mac_book_pro . , this may be true , and it does seem to have all the exact same i o ports in the same locations , including the mac " mini display connector " , but i do n't care , i like it . this laptop ( xps_15z ) , had one little quirk that threw me for a loop because i never had to deal with it before , but once i figured it out , i 'm really quite happy with it . that quirk is the " optimus " system that manages the two different graphics adapters , the low_power intel gpu , and the high power nvidia gpu . many linux users seek out systems with nvidia graphics , because nvidia likes linux , and in previous systems , i simply set the bios to only use the nvidia gpu . this laptop does not allow that option , forcing you to learn how to manage the optimus hardware . in a ms_windows system , virtually all of the applications have a profile file associated with it , and the os passes part of the profile to optimus , which determines if the high power nvidia gpu is needed . in linux , you have to use an application like " bumblebee " to manage optimus , and decide for yourself if the application you 're using requires the nvidia gpu . it 's really quite simple to create a launcher that starts your favorite apps . with the nvidia gpu enabled , but you have to know that it needs to be done . also , every high power 3d graphics app . that i 've tried so far , will actually run with only the intel gpu , just very slowly . under minimal power conditions ( display_brightness at minimum , keyboard back light off , wifi and bluetooth off , nothing plugged in to the usb ports , ethernet cable plugged in , intel gpu only ) , i get about 6 hrs . 20 mins . on the battery ... not bad . an interesting side note , simply turning on the nvidia gpu cuts that down to about 40 mins . , also the fan gets a little loud when nvidia is running full blast . addendum we have a huge fire burning here in so . cal . , and power lines got knocked down this morning , so we had a lengthy power failure . i kicked this laptop into low gear , connected it by tethering to my cell phone ( which means wifi ) , and i got over 7 hours_of_battery_life with the wifi turned on . apparently , wifi uses less power than wired ethernet on this machine . i 've jumped through all the hoops to get this thing running perfectly under linux ( fedora 18 ) , so if you 're considering this laptop as a linux machine , and need some help , just ask . by the way , there are a few misprints , even contradictions , in amazons' product_description . a couple of important notes that helped me decide to buy this machine are the nvidia gpu is a " geforce_gt 540m " , and the native resolution of the glass is a full 1920 x 1080 . for the geekier readers , here are a few numbers glxgears with intel gpu only glxgearsrunning synchronized to the vertical refresh . the framerate should be approximately the same as the monitor refresh_rate . 302 frames in 5.0 seconds 60 . 353 fps300 frames in 5.0 seconds 59 . 879 fps300 ( i prefer the club setting in the samsung settings with some minor_adjustments higher in the equalizer of the realtek speaker settings . ) ( major ) con the trackpad . the gold standard is the apple trackpad ( i have a macbook 15 " as well so i 'm very familiar with it ) . before getting into its flaws , on the plus side , when you are using the trackpad in a manner perfectly aligned with how samsung defined it must be used it works 95 as well as apple 's trackpad . 2 finger_scrolling works pretty well while browsing , but it 's not perfect . the first major problem is with basic operation . due to no physical_buttons , the driver must keep track of your thumb ( button ) position and figure out what you are trying to use it for resting it for a future button press or a 2 finger gesture . there is an invisible horizontal line between the lower button area of the trackpad and the main part of the trackpad . i 've measured the defined area at about 1cm high . if your thumb is resting in the button area , but drifts up the slightest bit off into the main area , the pointer will stop dead in its tracks , and activate the 2 finger gesture . the fact is that the button area is defined in software as too narrow . it 's very likely your thumb will drift if you typically rest your thumb ( button finger ) on the pad while moving around the pointer in normal use . just naturally rolling your thumb as your index_finger moves can trigger a pointer freeze . fyi , on the mac , the defined button area is wider so some drift is tolerated . ( plus i suspect apple 's driver is intelligent to know that 2 finger_scrolling does n't usually involve the thumb ) in fact , i never get pointer freeze on the mac , just to show the wide difference in performance . secondly , there is a bug in the trackpad driver itself . when you do drift up and freeze the pointer once or twice , it gets confused . when it 's confused it will frequently make the entire button area disappear for a short period of time for purposes of this algorithm . so , the result is if you are using 1 finger pointer movement and you so much as graze the button area of the trackpad the pointer will freeze . the button area should never trigger the start of a gesture . this combination of design flaw and bug causes constant pointer freezes in normal use . con 2 you will have to get used to a trackpad that is offset to the left side of the chassis . you basically have to unnaturally sit_in front of the left side of the screen instead of at the center . this is true for all keyboards with numerical keypads though . on this particular laptop it causes me to constantly be clicking the right button instead of the left as i 'm used to a centered trackpad . the divider between left and right button is an invisible line down the center . there is no intelligence whatsoever in deciding between left and right buttons . if you push near the middle you wo n't know what to expect . on a mac it knows that if i 'm moving around the pointer with my index_finger in the the right side of the pad that my thumb is still a left_click unless i move it to the right of my index_finger . ( because my thumb is oriented to the left of my index_finger ... while a right click causes my thumb to be to the right of it . ) ( ps i 'm anti apple , so holding up an apple superiority is unfortunate . but , these are problems samsung and its trackpad vendor can fix . ) these two cons are worth a 2 star drop because they are hidden flaws on a part of the laptop that is vital to user_experience . i 'll_update the review when these are addressed . if you only use an external_mouse , this is a 5 star laptop ! )
i really wanted to like this laptop , but a couple issues turned me away it 's got a high quality 17 . 3 " screen ( or as high quality as a tn panel will get you ) , a decently sized hdd , an onboard ssd that caches data from the hdd to improve_performance , a quality feel to the case , a terrific keyboard , and a long life battery ( 8 hours on a charge ! ) . unfortunately , in a room that 's at 23c ambient temperature , this laptop idles at a whopping 50c ( under load it gets just shy of 102c , and throttles down because of the temperature ) . the competing laptop sitting next to it idles at 35c ( and under load gets to 90c ) . these 50c and 99c temps are an immediate sign of a poor cooling mechanism in the samsung . i brought it back to the store i bought it from , and the technician said it was normal . no , that 's not normal and if it is then it 's a really poor_design . if you want a laptop that will last more than 3 years , or more than a month of solid gaming , you do not want it getting hot or any length of time . let 's say cooling was n't an issue only one ram module is accessible , and you ca n't upgrade it ( despite the ivy bridge cpu and competing models allowing higher density ram , this samsung only recognizes the 4gb module . ) one is stuck with 8gb which is plenty for most , but if you run virtual_machines or have other demanding software , you 're going to need more ... so if you do n't need to use more than 8gb_of_ram , while wanting a pretty paperweight or an expensive giant griddle to fry eggs and bacon on , this model might be perfect ...

when i think of lenovo laptops , the utilitarian , black plastic work computer always comes to mind . prior to lenovo 's purchase in 2005 , ibm originally designed the thinkpad , the iconic portable workhorse for business and industry , and no matter what hardware it has on the inside , the outside just said this computer is for work ! the laptop could have had the fastest processor and graphics_card , the latest technology , but lacked any fun and style . lenovo has changed that with the " ideapad " line of laptops . it is apparent that the " ideapad " is targeted to the consumer market rather than the businessman . unboxing the lenovo z570 is no " apple " event . i did not feel the need to get out my phone and record myself removing the laptop from its cardboard carton to post on youtube . i think that whole bit is a little self serving anyway , it 's like " look i have the latest gadget and you do n't " . in any event , the lenovo z570 is packaged like most computers . inside the cardboard box , which opens like a suitcase ( with a nice carry handle ) , you will find the laptop wrapped in a plastic bag cushioned between two soft foam protectors on each end . there is a white box containing the battery and the ac_adapter on the right side . there is also documentation , the most useful being a " setup poster v1 . 0 " , which shows how to install the battery , plug into ac , and turn the computer on , as well as diagrams for " buttons and functions " and " connections " . there are no discs included with the lenovo z570 , so you should make a backup of the factory default set right away , but more on that later . there is also no " user_guide " in print form included . the back of the setup poster says it can be accessed as a pre_loaded pdf file from an icon on your desktop . in my case the icon was there , but adobe reader was not installed , so the user_guide could not be read until i installed it , but i am getting way ahead of myself . also included are the " safety and general information guide " , " product specific notices " , which generally states the laptop is energy_star certified and fcc compliant , an accessory flyer , and a " lenovo limited_warranty " which in the us is 1 year parts and labor , and 1 year for the battery pack . the warranty is provided by " mail in service " or " customer replaceable unit " meaning they will ship out a part for free " for installation by you . " other countries provide different types of warranty service , but since i do n't live there it does not pertain to me . now , let 's take the z570 out of its plastic bag and take a look at it . the first thing to notice is the protective film on the top of the case . this protects it from any scratches . since i do n't want the laptop to look like my friend 's grandmother 's furniture when i was growing up i will remove that , when i do , i noticed another protective film covering the lenovo logo . i will remove that too . according to lenovo , the case color is gunmetal grey , although the bald guy from " pawn_stars " or an appraiser from " antiques_roadshow " would definitely tell you there is a patina to this grey . it has a slightly purpily brownish tint to it , it is not that pewtery dark grey that you think of as gunmetal . that does not mean it is not attractive , because it is , but the name is a little deceiving . the whole top ( the part that is the back of the screen when opened ) is this color and finished in a brushed_aluminum metal , with the exception of a black plastic panel at the top which swoops down . this undoubtedly holds the wi_fi antennas , since the aluminum would probably shield the signal causing poor reception . there is a lenovo logo in the upper_left corner ( looking towards the back of the screen ) . this logo does not light up like on other computer brands . that does n't matter to me . the body color fits in well at a cafe , it has almost a mocha espresso look to it , just do n't spill . when you open up the laptop the first thing you see is a thin piece of soft foam sandwiched between the screen and keyboard to protect them during shipping , as well as more protective film around the bezel , or frame of the screen . the frame is a glossy_black plastic that holds the screen in place . the top of it is slightly wider at an inch , while the sides are 3 4 of an inch . this is because the top holds the wireless antennas and the webcam . in the bottom left_hand_corner you see " z570 " printed just below the screen , reminding you of its model number , as well as a lenovo logo in the center . the keyboard has the same feel as the dell laptops , the secondary function key graphics are even printed in orange like dell 's , and the keys have a slight texture . the keys are slightly rounded , both on the very top so they scoop your finger , and the bottom edges ( dell 's does not have this ) . lenovo calls this an " accutype " keyboard . there is also a separate_numeric keyboard off to the right which is nice to have . typing on the keyboard is comfortable and natural , there is just enough tactile_response to let you know you have pressed the key . above the keyboard on the left side from left to right are a speaker , the power_button , the " one key rescue " button , three very small " pinhole " led 's to indicate , caps_lock , num_lock and hard_drive activity . the graphics printed next to each led to indicate their function are very hard to see unless you look directly on top of them , and that 's assuming there is no reflection to distract your vision . on the right side from left to right are buttons for mute , volume down , volume up , one key theater ii , thermal management , and another speaker . all of these buttons light up when the power is on . below the keyboard is the touchpad , which also has texture to it . if you look at it at an angle in the light you will see little raised dots that give it this feeling . i find the texture on the touchpad a little bit distracting , i prefer a smooth as glass touchpad like on the macbook pros , but you do get used it , and some people may prefer it . there is a one finger scroll function on the right side of the pad which is very useful when paging through large documents and websites . the performance of the touchpad on the lenovo z570 is very good , it responds well . i have tried the hp pavilion dv6 and the touchpad on that machine is terrible , it lags or does n't respond at all sometimes . the lenovo 's touchpad is far superior to the hp pavilion dv6 . below the touchpad is what looks like a single mouse button , but it is in fact two , depending on which side you actually click on , this also works well and is intuitive where to click even though nothing divides the two sides . on the very front of the lenovo z570 are four indicator led 's that indicate if the touchpad is turned off , the power is turned on , the battery status , and if the wi_fi is turned on . the graphics to indicate these functions are small like the other ones , but their placement in the front makes them a little easier to see , and the led 's are bigger and brighter . to the right of the led 's is a switch which turns the wi_fi on and off . considering most laptops either have a software switch , or a button on the keyboard a physical switch is pretty_nice because if you do not plan to use the wi_fi , you can turn off the radio prior to booting up the machine . to the right of the switch is a memory_card reader which will read the following types of cards secure_digital ( sd ) card , multimedia card ( mmc ) , secure_digital pro ( sd pro ) , memory stick pro ( ms_pro ) and xd picture ( xd ) cards . you will need to remove the dummy card before inserting another card . the right side of the machine has your headphone_and_microphone jacks , ( i should also note that there is a built_in_microphone about a half an inch below the keyboard on the left side . there is a tiny graphic with a pinhole there ) , two usb ports , an ethernet port and a dvd_rw drive . the dvd drive eject_button is sensitive . many times i have picked up the lenovo z570 and inadvertently opened the drive tray . this may cause damage if you do n't realize it has opened , go to move the laptop and tray opens causing you to lose your grip on that side . i could easily see the machine flying to the floor . the left side supplies a kensington slot ( lock not included ) to secure your laptop , the ac_power jack , the ventilation louvers for the system 's fan , a vga , hdmi , combo esata usb port and another usb port . all together there are four usb ports as long as you are not using an esata drive , if you are , then there are only three available . all usb ports are 2.0 not 3 . 0 , which is starting to become the new standard . there are no ports or hardware along the back side of this unit . now , let 's get to the specifications of the unit . the lenovo z570 that i am reviewing came with a second generation_intel_core i3 2350m processor running 2 . 30 ghz , 6 . 00 gb of ddr3 ram , an intel_hd_graphics 3000 adapter , a 5400 rpm 500 gb western_digital sata hard_drive , an optiarc dvd rw , a cyberlink 0.3 m web_cam , and realtec high definition audio , with srs surround_sound ( premium surround_sound ) . the display is a 15 . 6 inch led backlit thinkpad display with a maximum_resolution of 1366x768 . note that is not full 1080p resolution of 1920 x 1080 , but does exceed the 720p standard of 1280 x 720 . the wi_fi in this unit is 802 . 11n with backwards compatibility for b g as well . the wired ethernet connection only sports a_10 100 mbps speed , which is unfortunate , since gigabit connections are quickly becoming the standard in most households with the price of gigabit routers coming down and bandwidth use in most homes increasing . why lenovo would make the " wired " connection slower than the wireless speed is purely illogical . theoretically , your fastest network_connection is the wi_fi 802 . 11n connection on this laptop . there is also no bluetooth connection on the model that i tested , but similar lenovo models do offer this feature . there is also built in support for intel wireless display or widi , which allows simultaneous wireless display of what 's on your laptop 's screen to an hdtv if you have purchased the necessary receiver . since i do not have this receiver , i cannot comment on the performance of this technology . the battery_life is listed at up to five hours . i believe that this is fairly accurate . i have been using the ideapad solely on battery power , and i have yet to have the battery run out on me , but i have not used it for more than a few hours at a time , so the true run time is still unknown . ok , it 's time to turn on the ideapad and check out the performance of the z570 . the pre_installed operating system on this laptop is the 64 bit version of windows home_premium , which is pretty much the standard for most consumer oriented laptops . once the power_button is pressed , the universal symbol for power ( the circle with the line cutting through the top ) lights up in little pinpoint white dots , while the previously mentioned buttons above the keyboard also illuminate their functions in white led brilliance . initially windows 7 needs to be set up , creating a username , password , connecting to a network , etc . this will have to be done no matter what brand of computer purchased , it is a requirement of windows . after that is done , your desktop is displayed , and the laptop is ready to use . optimum viewing is within about a 30 degree angle of the machine from left to right , and a 100 to 125 degree angle up and down . it is best to look straight ahead and tilt the screen up or down until you get your best picture , otherwise the display looks really washed out . this is a problem with almost all backlit led screens i have seen with the exception of the mac_book_pro . the display has a glossy_finish like most laptop these days do , the colors are richly saturated , and text is crisp and sharp . lenovo does not include a lot of " bloat_ware " , or pre_installed programs , which in my opinion is a great thing , i like to install my own software , and usually there are nothing but trial_versions installed that make you dish out dollars if you want the full version anyway . the programs included are google_chrome , oovoo ( which is similar to skype ) , lenovo you cam ( webcam software ) , lenovo game_center , lenovo telephony ( voip links to poketalk ) , lenovo ee boot optimizer , lenovo veriface , cyberlink power2go ( cd_dvd burning software ) , one key recovery ( backup restore software ) and mcafee_antivirus plus trial . most of these programs i wo n't use except the youcam , one key recovery , and power 2 go . lenovo veriface uses the webcam to log you in based on a stored picture connected to your password . i had mixed results with this form of verification , unless the lighting is correct and the angle is right , it does n't really work , i would say i had about a 35 percent success rate . maybe if you do n't move your laptop , it will work better , but i tend to take it from room to room with varying lighting_conditions . the 802 . 11n wireless connection on the ideapad z570 is fast and furious , allowing for a great multimedia experience . netflix streaming was flawless , even in high definition , and the picture is stunning . even more stunning is the premium sound system on this machine . it has one of the best sounding audio systems that i have heard on a laptop . it plays loud and clear , and the spatial stereo separation is excellent . this is no doubt due to the built in srs surround_sound system . the one key theater button helps with making this experience even better . this is a touch_sensitive button , located above the keyboard which changes the brightness of the screen as well as the audio mode based the program being used . the " intelligent " mode works quite well , and that is the setting that i am keeping it on . the touch_sensitive volume_controls and mute button are right next to the one key theater button , and there is also an on screen display that pops up when you touch one of these buttons , similar to what you would see on your television . music sounds_great on the lenovo z570 , i enjoy watching music videos on youtube , and they look great , especially when you select 720p or even 1080p quality on the site . of course just playing audio tracks like on itunes is great as well . usually i would anticipate buying separate speakers to hook up a laptop for use at home , but that is not necessary for this computer ( unless you are looking for a lot of bass ) . for the average user the built in audio will be enough . it plays loud , is clear , and has decent frequency response for size of the drivers . if you plug in earphones , the lower frequencies missing from the speakers are represented , which would also be picked up on external_speakers depending on their quality of course . i could continue to comment on the lenovo ideapad z570 on and on , but i think this review is long enough already . overall i really enjoy this laptop . it is speedy , i cannot see much difference between the hp pavillion 's dv6 second generation i5_processor i have , and the second generation i3 in this laptop . it looks stylish , has a nice display and a great_sound system . its lack of bluetooth , usb 3 . 0 , and a gigabit_ethernet ports are the only downside to the z570 . other brands have some or all of those features on machines within the same price_range , so that is something to consider . pros brilliant 1366 x 768 hd_display with rich color saturationexcellent premium sound systemesata port for external hard drivefast wireless 802 . 11n speedcons lacks bluetoothlacks usb 3.0 supportlacks gigabit_ethernet port

from the big bulky monitors we 'd seen back in elementary_school , to the now ultra thin laptops carried around by many college students , apple has come a long way in molding the mac into what is now their ( arguably ) flagship product . but was this achieved solely through " cutting_edge " technology and innovations in computer science ? not really . and the reason why is because they 've created for themselves an air of smug and elitist attitudes for its consumers , achieved through their exorbitant and overpriced laptop specifications , hostile ad campaigns ( " i 'm a mac . and i 'm a pc " advertisements come to mind ) , and supposed revolutions in technology ( " retina display " was one such feature they 've touted as revolutionary , a feature advertised as bringing high resolution display . however , despite that , it was ibm who had actually invented the idea of a " retina display " , as early as 1998 ) . simply put , they 've cultivated for themselves the pinnacle of consumerist attitude . by buying into their appeal ( both literally and figuratively ) , you 've now become part of an " in group " of like minded people who believe they possess cutting_edge technology . but the product specifications are hardly cutting_edge , and neither is its value . see , what apple is infamous for that many of its consumers are unaware of , is that their specifications of a typical macbooks are usually weaker in comparison to their pc counterparts . for example , i 'll compare the basics specs of the current top of the line macbook , the macbook pro 13 . 3 inch , to the basic specs of a generic pc desktop that i 've found on newegg ( a website dealing in the market of computer goods ) , the avatar amd fx series ( link included at bottom ) . " priced at 589 , the pc desktop avatar amd fx series features 8gigabytes of ram , 3 . 3ghz processor , 1terabyte hard_drive space and an amd radeon hd 7770 graphics_card . priced at 1 , 049 , the macbook pro 13 . 3 inch boasts 4gigabytes of ram , 2 . 5ghz_processor , 500gb 's of hard_drive space and an intel_hd_graphics_4000 graphics_card . " for almost twice the cost of the pc desktop , you get almost half the power . and this is being generous with the generic desktop , as buying pre built desktops are actually significantly more expensive than assembling it yourself . upgrading the internal_hardware of a desktop_pc literally involves replacing whatever part you wanted to replace ( for example , going in and replacing its hard_drive or replacing an old ram stick ) . the cost ? whatever it cost you to buy that new part . the cost of " upgrading " a macbook ? however much it costs for an entirely new macbook , as apple does n't allow for the manual replacement of their hardware . another unfortunate reason to not invest in apple 's products are its awful working conditions set forth for its workers in their manufacturing plants . foxconn , a major multinational electronics manufacturing company , is one such company contracted by apple to produce their gadgets . foxconn has come under controversy for overworking their staff and cutting their wages . it 's gotten to the point where workers have to sign a document that states they will not make any attempt to commit suicide ( and several workers have made this attempt before . pictures taken of the exterior of foxconn buildings show that there is literally a thick webbing of rope outside every possible escape , designed so that it catches workers ) . while apple has made attempts to oversee this issue ( they 've hired the fair labors association to try and improve working conditions for foxconn ) , they seem to not do a very good job at handling things ahead of time pegatron , another manufacturing company , has been contracted to manufacture apple products . but unfortunately for apple , pegatron has recently come under fire for its use of child_labor in their manufacturing plants . and the final insult ? the viruses . macs were once touted as never needing to have antivirus_software , because of its supposed immunity to all sorts of infections . apple had no problem advertising this as yet another innovation of the standard macintosh product , and it worked the notion that your own computer would never be compromised by a malicious trojan or key logger was a huge selling_point to many computer illiterate people . but in reality ? viruses were able to infect mac products as much as their pc counterparts . the only reason they did n't at first were two key things 1 ) mac 's are closed_source , meaning , their source_code is n't widely available , which meant that it makes it difficult to make programs for macs ( in particular , viruses ) . 2 ) initially small market_share . because it was once a relatively unpopular product , there were n't many of them manufactured , which meant that not many people had them , which meant that there was n't an overall interest to create viruses for macs , as viruses are normally created usually for the purpose of stealing information . because the software was new ( and closed sourced ) , and because not many important businesses and or people initially used them , there was little to no interest to create viruses for macs . but now , as the number of people who own mac products grow , so too does the interest of creating trojans , key loggers and other malicious programs . when the first reports of mac viruses started cropping up ( one such infamous virus , the " macdefender " virus ) , some unfortunate consumers were initially confused about why their mac product had been acting up . some of these same consumers would end up calling tech_support on how to fix their product . apple 's response ? deny the existence of viruses . they had been so caught up in their " all powerful mac " hubris , that instead of owning up to what they had promised , they chose to not assist the same people who had put money into their products . fortunately , all that said , the typical mac product is n't without its upsides with an ingenious laptop cord design ( forcefully ejecting the cord from the laptop causes little risk of internal damage , as the end of the cord is a small magnetic strip ) , and with newer products becoming paper thin and lightweight , it 's not completely terrible . however , these do not completely make up for any of the faults it has . thus , that is why i 'm choosing to " think different " and stay with pc . not only do i get more out of my money with it , i also have more variety in what i 'm able to do with my pc , as the only real blunders i have to deal with is windows_8 . and even then , windows 8 is an optional upgrade . overall , i give the above macbook pro laptop , 2 stars out of 5 .

for a premium laptop sold in 2013 , the apple macbook pro ( 13 inch , base_model ) is about as basic as it gets no ssd , no discrete_graphics , no 1080p display , and no touch_screen . but apple does not pretend it has any of these . what it does have is great reliability on the software side and hardware side , apple 's osx mountain_lion , the sleek looks apple always delivers , reasonable specs , good battery_life , nice keyboard , and excellent trackpad . now , the question is , who is this computer for ? those looking for a bargain laptop will shy away from the enormous price_tag , and those who want to play the latest games do not ever use macs . the average computer user will be served better by a macbook air , since it is faster ( for basic tasks ) , lighter , and has a higher_res antiglare screen . the macbook pro 13 . 3 inch laptop is for those who want to use a mac , but value performance and upgradability over weight and screen_resolution . this mac will last longer than any other simply because it is the easiest to upgrade and repair . hard_drives can be replaced , ram can be added as needed , and the internal battery can be replaced after losing its ability to hold a charge . the processor is roughly 15 faster than the one inside the macbook air , which also extends this computer 's usable lifespan . the fact that the screen is fairly low_res for the price ( mbp_13 has a res of 1280x800 , while other windows laptops have a res of 1600x900 for the same price ) , really detracts from my personal_experience with the computer . the retina display of my iphone 5 has indeed spoiled me , and apple should update the screen of the mbp_13 or bring down the price of the retina model . this , added with the fact that the speed of the hard_drive is very slow for the money , detracts from the computer 's value . lowering the price by one hundred dollars would justify the hard_drive and screen and make the computer a five star purchase , but for the price , this is a four star ( good ) computer . those looking to drop 1200 on a new laptop will have to decide if the upgradability and processor performance is worth the money over the sleeker macbook air . in addition , if mac_osx is not something you enjoy using , then i would advise that you look elsewhere for a laptop . tldr version good , reliable laptop with mediocre screen and slow hard_drive .

i have already posted a similar review for the mbp old version , i am posting the same review here again since my review concentrates on the user_interface of os x . ( not too sure whether i am allowed to do post the same review but just thought it could help some people before they switch to os x ) i have been a windows user since i started using a computer and i never used a mac_os x till i actually bought the mbp in 2011 . so , this review would really help someone who is considering a mac for the first time and wants to use it either at school or to remotely connect to work . this article summarizes what you would love and what you could be missing . i previously_owned a desktop , a hp laptop and a compaq laptop before i bought a mbp . also , i still use windows machine at work . one of the major reasons i bought the mbp was because it was available on a ebay deal from macmall for 950 . i assumed that if i did not like it , i could always sell it for at least 850 on ebay or craigslist . before reading the next part , please do understand that mbp and os x come together . things you need to know os xswitching between applications this is one of my biggest quirks with os x . windows_7 does an awesome job in switching between applications . when you want to switch between the applications , you use alt_tab in windows_7 and this would shift the focus to the next application . if the application is minimized in os x , you can switch between applications by using cmd tab but it does not automatically bring up the other application , it just changes the active application in menu_bar . i never understood the reasoning behind this , why would i just want to see the menu_bar of the other application , i cannot imagine doing anything just with a menu_bar . after some search on the internet i found the work around to do this in os x . the answer is to press cmd tab followed by the option key ( just before releasing the cmd key ) to switch between the applications perfectly . you can also scroll your four fingers on the track pad to bring up all the applications and then highlight the application you want to choose to change the active application window . it is simply irritating to switch between keyboard and the track pad when you are typing some document or email . you can also use function key f11 instead of swiping the four fingers on the trackpad but at the end of the day windows 7 does a great_job here . please do note that you can only switch directly between applications but not directly to the active window of an application when you use cmd tab , for example you cannot switch directly to a open second excel workbook , you have to bring up the excel application first and only then can you switch to the second excel workbook . i am aware that there is software available ( namely witch for 14 ) to do this but i already paid for the machine and why should i go through all this trouble and change the system registry entries to simply switch between applications . we can also use spaces and assign some shortcuts to spaces ( like option arrow ) to make the switch between applications easier but you need to assign a different space to every application and this could be tedious after some time . also the animations could make you dizzy after a while ( not too sure whether everyone would share the same opinion ) and there is no way you can turn off these animations afaik . switching within an application to switch between the various windows of the same application , the answer is to press cmd , it works but what if i have 3 open excel workbooks . same answer as above , scroll the four fingers or press the function key f11 to see all active windows . taskbar could be a big_deal it is irritating not to have a task_bar in os x . you can never actually know that you had two open excel workbooks or two separate browser windows at a glance . to put this into context , try working in windows_7 grouping all your applications together all the time , in windows_7 the users have the option to ungroup individual windows by selecting " combine only when taskbar is full " in the taskbar properties . the problem with this approach in os x is that you will never know all the application windows unless you display all the active windows or highlight the application in the docking_bar . also , the docking_bar still occupies a substantial amount of screen space even in its minimal size , in windows_7 the taskbar is comparively small . due to the screen_size and resolution constraints we usually tend to hide this docking_bar on the 13 " mbp so that we can see the applications in the maximum available screen space . so either compromise on seeing the active applications in docking_bar or full screen mode for applications . again , the app witch is the answer for taskbar but it will display these active windows only when we press cmd tab . full screen i am addicted to seeing everything in maximized window mode in windows_7 machines , i could never be satisfied with the default resized small windows , so i installed a free application rightzoom to address this issue . so far , so good . quick links the docking_bar essentially acts likes the quick link shortcuts in windows_7 . cmd w closes the application and cmd q quits the application , you have to be careful enough not to press q instead of w . please note that closing a window does not automatically quit an application , the application is still active and consumes cpu resources . vpn connection certain ( or many ? ) vpn connection softwares like juniper cannot be installed on os x because some of these vpn connections connect using some plugins that are designed_specifically for internet explorer , which is not available on os x . i wanted to connect to work using the microsoft office remote_desktop client but could not do it due to this restriction . external applications all the applications cannot be installed in os x . there are lots of companies out there that make products just for windows machines . i had to install stattools for my course work and the tool was not available for os x , so i had to work from another windows machine at work on the weekends for my course work . i could have also installed bootcamp and that comes up next . bootcamp i installed windows_7 using bootcamp on mbp . i observed that windows_7 is slow and the hard_disk makes squeaky noises when you are trying to open an application in bootcamp , also the track pad experience is not the same despite the various drivers and the keyboard layout is obviously different . you can overcome these problems by connecting the mbp to a hdtv or any monitor and then using a wireless windows keyboard mouse but then the whole setup is too much hassle and defeats the purpose of a laptop . microsoft office the experience of using microsoft office on os x is pretty subpar in comparison to windows_7 , may be it the fault of microsoft but it is simply pretty_hard for someone to transition from office_2010 in windows_7 to office 2011 in os x . for example , i am used to zooming in and out of microsoft word using shortcuts like ctrl scroll up ( on trackpad ) and ctrl scroll down but this option is not available as shortcut in the os x version of office . i wanted to type a formula for a cell in excel and cannot find the formula bar . may be someone can help me if they know a way around enhancing this experience . delete_button there is no substitute to shift delete in os x ( cmd del ) . deletion followed by emptying trash is the only way to do it , if you are someone who is addicted to deleting the file at once there is no shortcut . cmd shift delete is a shortcut to empty trash after you delete something ( so two steps , not a major gripe ) . cut paste there is no such option as 'cut paste' in os x . if you want to move something to a different folder , you have to copy_and_paste the file into the target folder and then delete the original from the source folder . or select the file and carefully drag the file from the source into the target folder . preview preview can be used to apple store 's display does n't make it especially easy to compare the most significant differences among models , but it appears that the 15 " macbook_pro ( not the 15 " macbook_pro retina ) is the only current apple computer that comes with the following three features that are so essential to many us 1 . a built in optical_drive ( " superdrive " ) 2 . an " audio in " port 3 . an " audio out " port . with such a machine , any audiophile or media person is practically assured of having a self contained portable audio workstation , one that will record lps , cassette tapes , fm broadcasts with a simple line ( in my case , from an onkyo receiver ) to the " audio in " of the machine , nothing else required . moreover , the presence of the two ports permits near flawless capturing of any of the sounds emitted from a website or from the computer by attaching a simple patch cord between the two ports ( i use an inexpensive splitter at the " audio out " port for monitoring purposes . finally , the built in optical_drive obviates the need to drag along an external_drive , which can prove clumsy at best ( taking up extra_space on the desk ) and mal functioning at worst ( i 've never had a problem with an internal superdrive , but the external apple drives have failed with astonishing regularity , requiring all sorts of ingenious tricks to remove a stuck cd and often suffering damage in the process of removal ) . by contrast with this machine , the new imac ( and most of the other macbooks ) offers neither an optical_drive nor an " audio in " port . moreover , with the lack of an internal optical_drive , i 've forfeited two of the machine 's usb ports one to an interface the other , to a burner while attempting , with sporadic success , to import decent audio into the computer . solid_state_drive . the integrated solid_state_drive is amazingly_fast , and uses a 6 gb s sata connection right on the motherboard . it also allows for the incredibly thin form_factor . i 'm not sure , but it seems faster than normal solid_state_drives . the lack of a cabled connection should n't matter noticeably , so maybe it 's just my imagination . either way , it 's really nice to not have a spinning drive , and liberating to use a laptop without having to constantly worry about how much you 're moving the computer and wondering if you 're going to damage the drive . by the way here is how to pick out the right size drive spend a lot of time figuring out what kinds of things you 're going to do , and how much disk_space your media will take up , and how those needs are going to grow in the three to four years you own the computer . and then just order the largest drive available . trust me , you 'll thank me later . and even if you never come all that close to filling it , you
